cau_hoi: The report "Our Common Future" (1987) by the Brundtland Commission is famous for which definition?
A: Biodiversity is the number of bird species
B: Sustainable development: meeting current needs without compromising the ability of future generations to meet their own needs
D: Green economy means just planting trees
giai_thich: The commission was chaired by former Norwegian Prime Minister Gro Harlem Brundtland. The report emphasized that the environment, economy, and society are interconnected, and that poverty cannot be addressed while destroying nature, nor can nature be protected while ignoring poverty. The report led to the Earth Summit in Rio in 1992, where the Convention on Biological Diversity was signed.

cau_hoi: What is the significance of George Price's Price Equation (1970) in evolutionary biology?
C: Calculating the age of the Earth
D: It is a general mathematical formula describing the average change of a trait in a population over generations, separating components due to selection and transmission
giai_thich: The equation applies to any system with variation, heredity, and selection, not just genes but also culture. It helps clarify Hamilton's rule and selection at multiple levels. Price was a self-taught geneticist who worked with Hamilton and Maynard Smith in London. His life ended tragically in 1975, and his story is told in the book "The Price of Altruism."

cau_hoi: "Weismann's Barrier" (1892) proposed by German biologist August Weismann asserts what?
B: All cells can transform into sperm
D: Genetic information flows from germ cells to somatic cells, but changes in somatic cells do not revert back to germ cells
giai_thich: Weismann cut off the tails of mice over 22 generations (about 1,500 mice) and found that offspring still had normal tails, disproving Lamarck's idea of inherited acquired traits. He distinguished between the immortal "germ line" passed through generations and the "body" that will die. Today, scientists study epigenetics and find limited exceptions.

cau_hoi: In 2015, the decoding of the genomes of 120 Darwin's finches revealed which gene plays a major role in determining beak shape?
giai_thich: Leif Andersson's group and the Grants discovered different variants of the ALX1 gene associated with sharp or blunt beaks. In 2016, they further identified the HMGA2 gene affecting beak size, and this variant was strongly selected during the drought of 2004-2005 when large-beaked finches competed for large seeds. In humans, mutations in ALX1 cause facial deformities, indicating the same gene plays a role in shaping faces across many species.

cau_hoi: The three-spined stickleback in many freshwater lakes has lost its spiny pelvic bone. What genetic cause did scientists discover?
A: Due to the lake water being too cold
B: Loss of a segment of DNA controlling the activity of the Pitx1 gene in the pelvic region, while the gene itself remains functional in other parts
C: Due to fish eating less calcium
D: Complete loss of the Pitx1 gene
giai_thich: Marine sticklebacks have long pelvic spines to fend off predators. When they entered lakes after the Ice Age, where there were fewer predators but many insects that could snag the spines, losing the spines became advantageous. A 2010 study by David Kingsley showed that the "switch" DNA segment was lost independently in many different populations. This is a beautiful example showing that morphological evolution often comes from changes in gene regulatory regions, not the genes themselves.

cau_hoi: In freshwater three-spined sticklebacks, the bony armor plates on the body are rapidly decreasing. What interesting discovery was made about the Eda allele causing the reduction in armor?
A: This allele has existed at very low frequency in marine sticklebacks for millions of years, ready to be selected when fish enter freshwater
B: The allele appears completely new each time
C: The allele is only found in female fish
giai_thich: A 2005 study showed that the armor allele was rare in freshwater populations worldwide with an ancient origin, about 2 million years old. When marine fish entered lakes, this rare allele quickly increased due to selection. In Loberg Lake (Alaska), after fish were reintroduced in the 1990s, the allele frequency changed dramatically in just about 10 years. Such "reserve" variation allows evolution to occur very rapidly.

cau_hoi: According to Ernst Mayr (1954), how does "peripatric speciation" occur?
A: A small group of individuals at the edge of a distribution range becomes isolated, undergoes a founder effect and strong selection, and quickly forms a new species
B: A new species forms right in the middle of the original population
C: Species change simultaneously across the entire region
D: Two large species merge into one
giai_thich: Mayr was inspired by the kingfishers and birds of paradise in New Guinea and the surrounding small islands: populations on distant islands often differ the most. Small populations can change rapidly due to strong drift and new conditions, which Mayr called a "genetic revolution." This idea later became the foundation for Eldredge and Gould's punctuated equilibrium theory.
